chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz Al-Abdi, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Therefore whoever of you is present in the Month, he shall Fast therein.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'What can be clearer than it! The one who is present, so let him Fast it, and the one who travels, so he should not Fast it'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting for travelers according to the explanation of Surah Al-Baqarah verse 185?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a concise exegetical key to Surah Al-Baqarah 2:185, interpreting 'whoever is present' (man shahida) as a specific reference to those who are resident and not traveling. This narration establishes the foundational Shia legal principle that the exemption for travelers is not merely a concession but a direct application of the verse's wording, distinguishing between the obligation for the settled and the dispensation for the journeyer.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz Al Abdy, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘(What about) the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [2:185] therefore whoever of you is present in the Month, he shall Fast therein?’
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What can be clearer than it! The one who is present, so let him Fast it, and the one who travels, so he should not Fast it’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd al-’Aziz al-‘Abdiy from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘Whoever among you is present (at home) in the month of Ramadan must fast.’ [2:185]
He (the Imam) said, ‘It cannot be more vivid than this, those present must fast and those on a journey must not fast.’”
